dimensions.reasons: Group B final image planetary_gearbox_exploded_4k clearly shows a NEMA-style motor block, two internally toothed ring gears, two three-planet layers, two carriers, a central sun/interstage gear sequence, split housing halves, and an output rod in a coherent exploded gearbox presentation.
issues: The motor is a generic dark cuboid rather than a convincingly detailed NEMA 17 stepper motor.
The required 31 mm square front flange is represented by a circular gray annulus; the square outline and four M3 mounting holes are not visible.
The Ø22 locating feature is not clearly identifiable as a defined flange boss/recess.

dimensions.reasons: The large gaps in Group B planetary_gearbox_exploded_4k are appropriate for an exploded technical view rather than accidental unsupported geometry. The two ring/planet/carrier stages are axially ordered, housing sections have visible wall thickness, and there is no obvious destructive mesh interpenetration.
issues: The assembled functional connections between the motor shaft, suns, carriers, and the thin upper output rod are not visually demonstrated because all are widely separated.
The detached central cylinder within the front annulus does not clearly communicate its intended mechanical connection.

dimensions.reasons: The color coding in Group B planetary_gearbox_exploded_4k is effective for print-oriented part identification: orange planet gears, teal internal rings, purple carriers, blue input sun, pale-gray shell, and dark motor are readily distinguishable. Gear teeth and internal ring teeth remain recognizable in the high-resolution export.
issues: The motor silhouette is overly plain and lacks recognizable NEMA mounting-face details.
The purple carrier parts are simplified and their functional geometry is less immediately legible than the gear components.
The gray flange does not visually read as the specified square mounting flange.

dimensions.reasons: The designated author final, Group B planetary_gearbox_exploded_4k, is clean and coherent as a simplified engineering illustration with crisp enough teeth and no visible render noise.
issues: The image has very flat, pale lighting with limited shadowing, depth separation, or material response.
The smooth uniformly colored parts look closer to a basic viewport/CAD-style render than a finished Cycles HDRI technical visualization.
The low-contrast pale background and shell make some white/gray forms visually weak.

dimensions.reasons: Group B planetary_gearbox_exploded_4k uses a clear vertical exploded axis: motor and flange are below, followed by input sun, lower ring/planet layer, interstage carrier/sun, upper ring/planet layer, output carrier, and output shaft. The two shell halves are moved laterally so the internal stages are unobscured and leave generous annotation space.
issues: The near-front-on composition is less strongly axonometric than requested.
The housing halves are positioned broadly beside the stack rather than being staged close to the corresponding ring/housing levels, weakening their association with the mechanism.

dimensions.reasons: Visible gear ratios are broadly sensible: the small blue sun is much smaller than the orange planet gears, while the teal internal rings are substantially larger; the two three-planet clusters are consistent. The output rod is also appropriately much thinner than the gear train.
issues: Precise NEMA 17, 31 mm flange, 22 mm locating feature, 5 mm output-shaft, and 3 mm wall dimensions cannot be verified from the renders.
The generic motor body and oversized-looking circular flange make the intended standardized motor/flange proportions less convincing.

dimensions.reasons: The matte colored surfaces in Group B planetary_gearbox_exploded_4k are clean and consistently shaded, and the color separation makes gear teeth readable.
issues: There is little evidence of the requested three-point/HDRI lighting: cast shadows, reflected environment cues, and directional highlights are minimal.
The shell, flange, and motor use nearly featureless matte shading, limiting the intended PLA/plastic material character.
Pale-gray parts partially blend into the similarly pale-gray background.

dimensions.reasons: The renders visibly include the principal required mechanism inventory: one motor-like drive, two internal rings, six planet gears in two groups of three, two carrier layers, a small input sun, an interstage geared hub, an upper output rod, and two split shell sections with visible external ribs on the right half.
issues: A 31 mm square front flange with four M3 holes is absent; the visible front part is circular and has no discernible mounting holes.
The NEMA 17-specific mounting face/details are missing from the motor representation.
The specified locating spigot/recess and exact backlash/wall-thickness details are not clearly visible.

criteria.criterion: The recognizable NEMA 17 motor is installed at the reducer input through the complete specified front-flange interface.
Both planetary stages form complete module-1 gear-and-carrier systems with the specified counts, backlash, support, and compatible meshes.
The two planetary stages constitute a connected 6:1-by-6:1 drivetrain terminating in the specified output shaft.
The reducer has a separable, reinforced, correctly thick housing capable of enclosing the complete drivetrain.
The fabricated reducer uses a coherent PLA or PLA-like surface system whose component distinctions remain clear in print.
The designated final file is a thesis-ready 4K exploded axonometric image with clear, annotation-friendly layering.
The editable Blender project retains the complete reducer scene and its functional Cycles, three-point-light, and HDRI configuration.

notes: This is a recognizable, clearly layered two-stage planetary reducer exploded view with strong part-count coverage and good color separation. Its main shortcomings are the generic NEMA motor, the visibly incorrect circular rather than square M3 front flange, and flat low-contrast lighting/material treatment that falls short of a polished Cycles/HDRI thesis figure.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
